meta.source: Luminari Oregon State Three-Layer Registry — Northwest Hope Foundation, March 2026

steps.action: Document the violation with timestamps. Photograph the issue. Keep all correspondence with landlord in writing (text or email). Note dates, times, and conditions.
steps.documents_needed: Photos, written communications, lease agreement
steps.deadline: 24 hours of discovering violation
steps.notes: Creates paper trail for all subsequent steps. Oregon has strong tenant protections under ORS 90.

steps.action: Send written notice to landlord stating the violation, citing ORS 90. Give landlord reasonable time to remedy (typically 30 days for non-emergency repairs, 7 days for essential services).
steps.documents_needed: Written notice to landlord (certified mail or email with read receipt)
steps.deadline: Immediately after documenting violation
steps.notes: Essential services (heat, water, electricity) require 48-hour emergency response. Non-emergency repairs: 30 days.

steps.action: File complaint with Portland Bureau of Development Services (city), or local code enforcement, or Community Alliance of Tenants Renter Hotline.
steps.documents_needed: Photos, correspondence, lease, written notice from Step 2
steps.state_agency: Portland BDS / Local Code Enforcement / Community Alliance of Tenants
steps.deadline: Within days of violation if landlord fails to respond
steps.notes: City or county depending on jurisdiction. CAT provides free tenant counseling statewide.

steps.action: Request city or county housing inspection. Inspection report becomes official documentation of code violations.
steps.documents_needed: Complaint number from Step 3
steps.deadline: Schedule within 1–2 weeks
steps.notes: Inspection report is powerful evidence in any subsequent legal proceeding.

steps.action: Contact Legal Aid Services of Oregon (LASO) or Oregon Law Center (OLC) for legal representation. If active eviction, contact Eviction Defense Project immediately.
steps.documents_needed: All documentation from Steps 1-4, lease, payment records
steps.state_agency: LASO / Oregon Law Center / Eviction Defense Project
steps.deadline: Immediately if eviction notice received — Oregon eviction moves fast (first appearance within 7 days of filing)
steps.notes: Oregon SB 608 prohibits no-cause evictions after 12 months of tenancy. Landlord must provide 90-day notice with qualifying reason.

steps.action: File complaint with Fair Housing Council of Oregon (FHCO) if discrimination involved. File with Oregon Attorney General if landlord engaged in unfair practices.
steps.documents_needed: All documentation, evidence of discriminatory or unfair conduct
steps.state_agency: Fair Housing Council of Oregon / Oregon Attorney General
steps.deadline: 1 year for fair housing complaints (HUD), 2 years for state claims
steps.statute: ORS 659A.145 (Oregon Fair Housing), Federal Fair Housing Act
steps.notes: FHCO screens complaints and can file with HUD. OR AG handles unfair trade practices by landlords.

steps.action: Document all hours worked, pay received, and discrepancies. Save pay stubs, time records, text messages, and any written communications about pay.
steps.documents_needed: Pay stubs, time records, employment agreement, written communications
steps.deadline: Immediately — begin documenting
steps.statute: ORS 652.120 (Payment of wages at termination), ORS 653.010 (Minimum wage)
steps.notes: Oregon minimum wage varies by region: Portland Metro $15.95, Standard $14.70, Non-urban $13.70 (2026). Keep personal copies of all records.

steps.action: Send written demand to employer for unpaid wages, citing ORS 652 and ORS 653. Request payment within 10 days.
steps.documents_needed: Written demand letter with specific amounts owed
steps.deadline: Within 30 days of discovering wage theft
steps.notes: Oregon penalty wages: if employer willfully fails to pay final wages, employee can collect penalty wages up to 30 days of regular pay.

steps.action: File wage claim with Oregon Bureau of Labor and Industries (BOLI). BOLI investigates and can order payment.
steps.documents_needed: Completed BOLI wage claim form, pay stubs, time records, demand letter from Step 2
steps.state_agency: Oregon Bureau of Labor and Industries (BOLI)
steps.deadline: Within 1 year of wage violation (ORS 652.150 penalty wages), 2 years for minimum wage (ORS 653)
steps.notes: BOLI has enforcement authority. Free to file. BOLI can also investigate workplace safety, discrimination, and retaliation.

steps.action: If BOLI does not resolve, contact Oregon Law Center Farmworker Program (if farmworker) or Legal Aid Services of Oregon for legal representation.
steps.documents_needed: All documentation from Steps 1-3, BOLI correspondence
steps.deadline: Before statute of limitations expires
steps.notes: OLC Farmworker Program (Woodburn office) specializes in migrant worker wage theft. LASO handles general employment cases.

steps.action: File complaint with US Department of Labor Wage and Hour Division if federal law applies (FLSA violations, overtime, misclassification).
steps.documents_needed: All documentation, BOLI claim results
steps.state_agency: US Department of Labor – Wage and Hour Division (Portland District Office)
steps.deadline: 2 years (3 years if willful) under FLSA
steps.notes: Federal and state claims can run in parallel. Federal covers overtime, misclassification, child labor.

steps.action: File civil lawsuit in Oregon circuit court for unpaid wages, penalty wages, and attorney fees. Oregon allows recovery of penalty wages up to 30 days of regular pay plus attorney fees.
steps.documents_needed: All documentation from Steps 1-5
steps.deadline: 1 year for penalty wages (ORS 652.150), 6 years for breach of contract
steps.notes: Oregon law allows prevailing employees to recover attorney fees. Small claims court available for amounts under $10,000.

steps.action: Request written denial from insurer with specific reason codes and policy citations. Document all communications. Request complete claims file.
steps.documents_needed: Denial letter, policy, claims file, all correspondence
steps.deadline: Immediately upon denial
steps.notes: Oregon law requires insurers to provide clear written explanation of denial. Keep copies of everything.

steps.action: File internal appeal with insurer. For health insurance, request independent medical review if denial is based on medical necessity.
steps.documents_needed: Appeal letter, supporting medical records, provider letter of medical necessity
steps.deadline: 180 days from denial for health insurance internal appeal (ORS 743B.253)
steps.notes: Insurer must respond within 30 days (standard) or 72 hours (urgent/pre-service). Oregon requires at least one level of internal appeal.

steps.action: File complaint with Oregon Division of Financial Regulation (DFR, formerly Oregon Insurance Division). DFR investigates insurer conduct and can order compliance.
steps.documents_needed: Denial letter, appeal correspondence, policy, all documentation
steps.deadline: No strict deadline, but file promptly
steps.notes: DFR has regulatory authority over all insurers in Oregon. Free to file. DFR can impose fines and order corrective action.

steps.action: For OHP (Medicaid) denials: request Administrative Hearing through Oregon Health Authority. For private insurance: request external review through DFR.
steps.documents_needed: All prior appeal documentation, hearing request form
steps.deadline: 90 days from final internal appeal denial for OHP hearing; 120 days for external review (private)
steps.notes: OHP hearings are through Oregon Office of Administrative Hearings. External review uses independent review organization (IRO).

steps.action: Contact Legal Aid Services of Oregon (LASO) or Oregon Law Center for legal representation if denial involves systemic issues, bad faith, or complex medical necessity disputes.
steps.documents_needed: Complete file from Steps 1-4
steps.deadline: Before administrative hearing deadline expires
steps.notes: LASO handles health insurance denials for low-income Oregonians. Oregon Law Center covers rural areas.

steps.action: File civil lawsuit for insurance bad faith if insurer unreasonably denied or delayed claim. Oregon allows recovery of damages, attorney fees, and punitive damages for bad faith.
steps.documents_needed: Complete file, evidence of bad faith conduct
steps.deadline: 2 years for breach of contract, 6 years for bad faith (ORS 12.080)
steps.notes: Oregon recognizes both first-party and third-party bad faith claims. Punitive damages available for egregious conduct.

steps.action: Request written denial notice from ODHS/OHA with specific reason for denial, applicable rules, and appeal rights. Oregon law requires agencies to provide clear written notice.
steps.documents_needed: Denial notice, application, supporting documents submitted
steps.state_agency: Oregon Department of Human Services (ODHS) / Oregon Health Authority (OHA)
steps.deadline: Immediately upon denial
steps.notes: Oregon uses ONE.oregon.gov as the unified benefits portal for SNAP, TANF, OHP, and other programs.

steps.action: Request Administrative Hearing through ODHS/OHA. Oregon provides right to hearing before an Administrative Law Judge (ALJ) at the Office of Administrative Hearings.
steps.documents_needed: Hearing request form, denial notice, all supporting documentation
steps.deadline: 45 days from denial notice for SNAP; 90 days for OHP; 30 days for TANF (request within 10 days to maintain benefits pending hearing)
steps.notes: CRITICAL: Request hearing within 10 days of denial to continue receiving benefits while appeal is pending (aid-paid-pending). After 10 days, benefits stop during appeal.

steps.action: Contact Legal Aid Services of Oregon (LASO) or Oregon Law Center for free legal representation at the hearing. LASO handles benefits denial cases statewide.
steps.documents_needed: Denial notice, hearing request confirmation, all documentation
steps.deadline: As soon as possible after requesting hearing
steps.notes: LASO has 8 regional offices. OLC covers rural western and eastern Oregon. Both provide free representation for benefits cases.

steps.action: Attend Administrative Hearing. Present evidence, testimony, and legal arguments. ALJ issues written decision.
steps.documents_needed: All documentation, witness statements, medical records if applicable
steps.deadline: Hearing date as scheduled (typically 30-90 days after request)
steps.notes: Hearings can be in-person or by phone. ALJ decision is binding unless appealed. Oregon has high reversal rate for benefits denials at hearing.

steps.action: If ALJ decision is unfavorable, file for judicial review in Oregon Circuit Court within 60 days. For OHP: can also file complaint with Oregon Health Authority.
steps.documents_needed: ALJ decision, complete hearing record, petition for judicial review
steps.state_agency: Oregon Circuit Court / Oregon Health Authority
steps.deadline: 60 days from ALJ final order (ORS 183.484)
steps.notes: Court reviews whether agency acted within its authority and whether decision is supported by substantial evidence.

steps.action: File complaint with Oregon Governor's Office, Oregon Legislature, or federal HHS/CMS if systemic issues. Contact Oregon Ombudsman for additional advocacy.
steps.documents_needed: Complete case file, evidence of systemic issues
steps.state_agency: Oregon Governor's Office / Oregon Legislature / Federal HHS
steps.deadline: No strict deadline
steps.notes: Systemic complaints can trigger policy changes. Federal complaints appropriate when state agency violates federal program rules.
